findings.summary: A restarted generation destroys its own launch and review facts -- the same defect the resume rehydration was added to fix, on the other path that rebuilds the data plane. Rehydration is gated on `resume` alone (dd_runner.py:347), but generation n+1 is the control plane's normal exit from any non-complete terminal (control_plane.py:150-156, 438-446; run_root `g{n}` makes prior_generation_state_roots non-empty at dd_replay.py:497, so build_pipeline installs the ReceiptReplayer at dd_runner.py:129-145). For every replayed stage the walker enters the sealed receipt and 'no actor runs' (dd_pipeline.py:449-462), so AgentRunStageActor._record_cost_obs never fires and no launch/review fact is emitted. The exposition filename derives from development_id only (dd/cost_obs.py:51-60), so dd_runner.py:376 then unconditionally overwrites generation 1's `cost-obs-<development>.prom` with promotion + settlement + management alone. The loss is fully silent: mark_absent_if_missing runs only on non-complete terminals (dd_pipeline.py:347-348), so a generation 2 that completes emits no `cost_obs_lifecycle_present{lifecycle="launch"} 0` either -- absent data is neither present nor explicitly missing, which is exactly the distinction spec requirement 3 exists to create. `sum(cost_obs_launch_total)` and `sum(cost_obs_review_total{phase=~"continuous|final"})` under-count precisely the developments that needed a restart, and rule 5's `on(order_id)` join finds no launch series for that settled order, so the exact-once reconciliation rule emits nothing for it -- the silent-rule failure spec requirements 1, 2 and 4 exist to end. No test covers a generation-2 run's cost facts; TestWaitingOnAHumanAndComingBack only pins resume=True.

`cost_obs_execution_cost_total` carries only an `attribution` label (data_plane.py:182-187), so it cannot accumulate across the per-development files the design now requires. Every development renders its own `cost-obs-<development>.prom` into one shared node_exporter textfile directory (dd/cost_obs.py:51-60; deploy/prometheus/cost-observability.yml:19-24 states the fleet total accumulates because node_exporter serves them all), and every one of those files contains the byte-identical series `cost_obs_execution_cost_total{attribution="management"}` / `{attribution="launch"}` / `{attribution="unknown"}`. node_exporter re-exposes the whole directory through one registry, so two developments' spend is the same series twice: the duplicate is dropped at gather time (and a served duplicate would fail the Prometheus scrape for the target outright). Rule 1's numerator and denominator therefore both silently under-count fleet-wide, and the explicit `unknown` bucket spec requirement 3 asks to keep visible survives for only one development at a time. The code shows the constraint was understood one scope too narrowly: samples() dedup-sums identical label sets precisely so the cost metric is 'not a duplicate that a scrape would reject' (data_plane.py:228-231), but that merge is per-file. Every other source fact carries `order_id` and does accumulate; the cost metric alone has no per-order or per-development dimension. TestDevelopmentsAccumulateInOneExpositionDirectory only exercises LAUNCH_METRIC across files, which is why this is invisible to the suite.

Nothing in the shipped deployment turns collection on. The control plane's launch argv never passes `--cost-obs-dir` (control_plane.py:438-446 has no cost-obs flag), so the run falls back to FLEET_GRAPH_COST_OBS_DIR, and the shipped systemd unit sets no such Environment= line -- only the optional `EnvironmentFile=-%h/.config/fleet-graph/env`. The requirement is documented in deploy/prometheus/cost-observability.yml, and an operator-supplied env file is a legitimate site-config seam, so this is not counted against the spec; it is flagged because a deploy that folds in the Prometheus fragment but misses the env line gets five healthy rules over an empty textfile directory, which is the exact symptom this development was opened to end.
